source_refs.note: Section 14.2 heading (PDF 17); the section has no text of its own before 14.2.1, so this topic introduces the two mechanisms described in 14.2.1 and the hormonal section.

blocks.text: The kidneys can make urine that is more concentrated or more dilute than the blood. When the body needs to save water they excrete hypertonic urine; when there is much water in the body they excrete hypotonic urine.

Two mechanisms control this: the counter-current mechanism of the loop of Henle, which keeps the medulla salty, and the hormones ADH and aldosterone, which adjust how much water and salt the distal tubule and collecting duct take back.
